subproblem.title: Carrier side: ∫_{g(A)} J_T·h dH^n = ∫_A |det D(G∘g)|·h∘g dL^n via the Jacobian chain rule (parent steps 5–6)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ; g : ℝ^n → ℝ^P Lipschitz; A ⊆ ℝ^n Borel with g injective on A and differentiable at every point of A; V ⊆ ℝ^P open with g(A) ⊆ V; F, G : ℝ^P → ℝ^n with F = G on V and F differentiable at every point of g(A); T : ℝ^P → {linear subspaces of ℝ^P} with T(g(a)) = range Dg(a) for L^n-a.e. a ∈ A (Dg(a) = fderiv ℝ g a); and h : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] arbitrary (no measurability assumed). For x ∈ ℝ^P let J_T(x) := (det(⟨DF(x)u_i, DF(x)u_j⟩)_{i,j})^{1/2}, where DF(x) = fderiv ℝ F x and (u_i) is the standard orthonormal basis (stdOrthonormalBasis) of T(x), indexed by Fin(dim T(x)). Then ∫_{g(A)} J_T(x)·h(x) dH^n(x) = ∫_A |det D(G∘g)(a)|·h(g(a)) dL^n(a), where H^n = μHE[n], L^n = volume on ℝ^n, D(G∘g)(a) = fderiv ℝ (G∘g) a regarded as a linear endomorphism of ℝ^n, and both factors J_T and |det D(G∘g)| enter through ENNReal.ofReal.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (g : Euclid n → Euclid P) (A : Set (Euclid n)) (Lg : NNReal) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (F G : Euclid P → Euclid n) (T : Euclid P → Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (h : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞), LipschitzWith Lg g → MeasurableSet A → InjOn g A → (∀ a ∈ A, DifferentiableAt ℝ g a) → IsOpen V → g '' A ⊆ V → EqOn F G V → (∀ x ∈ g '' A, DifferentiableAt ℝ F x) → (∀ᵐ a ∂(volume.restrict A), T (g a) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ g a : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P)) → ∫⁻ x in g '' A, ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin (Module.finrank ℝ (T x)) => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ F x (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ (T x) i)) (fderiv ℝ F x (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ (T x) j))))) * h x ∂μHE[n] = ∫⁻ a in A, ENNReal.ofReal |LinearMap.det (fderiv ℝ (G ∘ g) a : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid n)| * h (g a) ∂volume
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5 and 6 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 3 §2, (2.4)–(2.5): along the parametrized piece the tangential Jacobian of F times the Jacobian of the parametrization g is the Jacobian of F∘g = G∘g; combined with the injective Lipschitz area formula of Simon Ch. 2 §3). Notation: λ := volume on ℝ^n; H^n := μHE[n] on ℝ^P; for linear maps, normDet is Mathlib's LinearMap.normDet (≥ 0, normDet_nonneg); areaJacobianAt ψ a = normDet(Dψ(a)) (SimonGMT areaJacobianAt_eq_normDet; import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz). Library facts: (A2) for a Lipschitz ψ : E → E' between finite-dimensional real inner product spaces, a Borel s ⊆ E on which ψ is injective and an arbitrary κ : E' → [0, ∞], ∫_{ψ(s)} κ dμHE[finrank ℝ E] = ∫_s ofReal(areaJacobianAt ψ a) · κ(ψ(a)) dλ(a) (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn); (G1) for linear L : U → W' and B : W' → W'', normDet(B ∘ L) = normDet(B.domRestrict (range L)) · normDet(L) (LinearMap.normDet_comp); (G2) for linear f : U → W' and an orthonormal basis b of U, normDet(f)^2 = det(Matrix.gram ℝ (f ∘ b)) = det(⟨f b_i, f b_j⟩)_{i,j} (LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram; over ℝ the coercion ℝ → ℝ is the identity, RCLike.ofReal_real_eq_id); (D) normDet(f) = |det f| for an endomorphism f of a finite-dimensional real inner product space (LinearMap.normDet_eq_abs_det).
1. (Gram identity.) Let B : ℝ^P → ℝ^n be linear and S, W ⊆ ℝ^P subspaces with S = W, and let u := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ S. Applying (G2) to f := B.domRestrict S (whose value at u_i is B u_i) and b := u gives normDet(B.domRestrict S)^2 = det(⟨B u_i, B u_j⟩)_{i,j}. As normDet ≥ 0, Real.sqrt_sq gives sqrt(det(⟨B u_i, B u_j⟩)_{i,j}) = normDet(B.domRestrict S) = normDet(B.domRestrict W).
2. (Injective area formula for g.) Apply (A2) with ψ := g (Lipschitz), s := A (Borel, g injective on A) and κ(x) := ofReal(J_T(x)) · h(x) (no measurability of κ is needed). Since finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), μHE[finrank ℝ ℝ^n] = μHE[n], and we get ∫_{g(A)} ofReal(J_T(x)) · h(x) dH^n(x) = ∫_A ofReal(areaJacobianAt g a) · (ofReal(J_T(g(a))) · h(g(a))) dλ(a).
3. (Reduction to an a.e. pointwise identity.) By lintegral_congr_ae it suffices to show, for λ⌞A-a.e. a, that ofReal(areaJacobianAt g a) · (ofReal(J_T(g(a))) · h(g(a))) = ofReal(|det D(G∘g)(a)|) · h(g(a)). By the hypothesis on T and ae_restrict_mem (A is Borel), λ⌞A-a.e. a satisfies a ∈ A and T(g(a)) = range Dg(a). Fix such an a and put x := g(a) ∈ g(A) ⊆ V, L := Dg(a), B := DF(x).
4. (G is differentiable at x with DG(x) = B.) V is open and x ∈ V, so V is a neighbourhood of x (IsOpen.mem_nhds) on which F = G; hence F and G agree eventually near x (Filter.eventuallyEq_of_mem). F is differentiable at x (x ∈ g(A)), so G is differentiable at x (DifferentiableAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq) and DG(x) = DF(x) = B (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).
5. (Chain rule.) g is differentiable at a (a ∈ A), so by fderiv_comp, D(G∘g)(a) = DG(x) ∘ Dg(a) = B ∘ L, also as linear maps (ContinuousLinearMap.toLinearMap_comp).
6. (Jacobian factorization.) By (D), |det D(G∘g)(a)| = normDet(B ∘ L). By (G1), normDet(B ∘ L) = normDet(B.domRestrict (range L)) · normDet(L). By step 1 with S := T(x) and W := range L (equal by the choice of a), normDet(B.domRestrict (range L)) = sqrt(det(⟨B u_i, B u_j⟩)_{i,j}) with u the standard orthonormal basis of T(x), which is J_T(x). Also areaJacobianAt g a = normDet(L). Hence |det D(G∘g)(a)| = J_T(g(a)) · areaJacobianAt g a.
7. (The integrands agree.) Since J_T(g(a)) = sqrt(…) ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_mul gives ofReal(J_T(g(a)) · areaJacobianAt g a) = ofReal(J_T(g(a))) · ofReal(areaJacobianAt g a). Therefore ofReal(|det D(G∘g)(a)|) · h(g(a)) = ofReal(J_T(g(a))) · ofReal(areaJacobianAt g a) · h(g(a)), which equals ofReal(areaJacobianAt g a) · (ofReal(J_T(g(a))) · h(g(a))) by commutativity and associativity in [0, ∞] (ring).
8. (Conclusion.) By steps 3–7 the two integrands of step 2 agree λ⌞A-a.e., so ∫_{g(A)} ofReal(J_T(x)) · h(x) dH^n(x) = ∫_A ofReal(|det D(G∘g)(a)|) · h(g(a)) dλ(a). ∎
proof_key_steps: Gram identity: for u the standard orthonormal basis of S = W, sqrt(det(⟨B u_i, B u_j⟩)) = normDet(B.domRestrict W) (normDet_sq_eq_det_gram, normDet ≥ 0).
The injective Lipschitz area formula (A2) for g with the arbitrary weight ofReal(J_T)·h gives ∫_{g(A)} ofReal(J_T)·h dH^n = ∫_A ofReal(areaJacobianAt g)·ofReal(J_T∘g)·h∘g dλ.
For a.e. a ∈ A with T(g(a)) = range Dg(a): F = G near g(a), so DG(g(a)) = DF(g(a)) and D(G∘g)(a) = DF(g(a))∘Dg(a).
|det D(G∘g)(a)| = normDet(DF(g(a))∘Dg(a)) = normDet(DF(g(a))|_{range Dg(a)})·normDet(Dg(a)) = J_T(g(a))·areaJacobianAt g a (normDet_eq_abs_det, normDet_comp, Gram identity).
ENNReal.ofReal_mul and lintegral_congr_ae identify the two integrals.

subproblem.title: Fibre side: the Euclidean weighted area formula for Φ transported through the injective parametrization g (parent steps 3–4)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ; g : ℝ^n → ℝ^P continuous; A ⊆ ℝ^n Borel with g injective on A; F : ℝ^P → ℝ^n; Φ : ℝ^n → ℝ^n Lipschitz with F(g(a)) = Φ(a) for every a ∈ A; and h : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] Borel measurable. Then the fibre-sum function y ↦ Σ_{x ∈ g(A), F(x) = y} h(x) (the tsum over the subtype g(A) ∩ F^{−1}{y}) is a.e. measurable for Lebesgue measure L^n (volume) on ℝ^n, and ∫_{ℝ^n} Σ_{x ∈ g(A), F(x) = y} h(x) dL^n(y) = ∫_A |det DΦ(a)| · h(g(a)) dL^n(a), where DΦ(a) = fderiv ℝ Φ a regarded as a linear endomorphism of ℝ^n and the factor |det DΦ(a)| enters through ENNReal.ofReal.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (g : Euclid n → Euclid P) (A : Set (Euclid n)) (F : Euclid P → Euclid n) (Φ : Euclid n → Euclid n) (LΦ : NNReal) (h : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞), Continuous g → MeasurableSet A → InjOn g A → LipschitzWith LΦ Φ → (∀ a ∈ A, F (g a) = Φ a) → Measurable h → AEMeasurable (fun y : Euclid n => ∑' x : ↥(g '' A ∩ F ⁻¹' {y}), h x) volume ∧ ∫⁻ y, (∑' x : ↥(g '' A ∩ F ⁻¹' {y}), h x) ∂volume = ∫⁻ a in A, ENNReal.ofReal |LinearMap.det (fderiv ℝ Φ a : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid n)| * h (g a) ∂volume
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3 and 4 of the parent proof (the carrier fibre over y is the g-image of the parameter fibre of Φ = G∘g over y, and the Euclidean weighted area formula, Simon Ch. 2 §3 (3.4)–(3.5) as formalized in SimonGMT, applies to the Lipschitz map Φ : ℝ^n → ℝ^n with the Borel weight h∘g). Here Φ is any Lipschitz map with F∘g = Φ on A; the parent applies this with Φ := G∘g. Notation: λ := volume on ℝ^n. SimonGMT definitions (import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaNoninjective): areaFiber A Φ y := {a // a ∈ A ∧ Φ a = y}; weightedAreaFiberSum A Φ w y := Σ_{a : areaFiber A Φ y} w(a) (tsum); areaJacobianAt Φ a = normDet(DΦ(a)) (areaJacobianAt_eq_normDet). Library fact (A1): for a Lipschitz map Φ between finite-dimensional real inner product spaces E → E', a Borel set A ⊆ E and a Borel w : E → [0, ∞], the function weightedAreaFiberSum A Φ w is μHE[finrank ℝ E]-a.e. measurable (aemeasurable_weightedAreaFiberSum_lipschitz) and ∫ weightedAreaFiberSum A Φ w y dμHE[finrank ℝ E](y) = ∫_A ofReal(areaJacobianAt Φ a) · w(a) dλ(a) (weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_fiberSum). Library fact (E): μHE[finrank ℝ E] = volume on E = ℝ^n (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Library fact (D): for an endomorphism f of a finite-dimensional real inner product space, normDet(f) = |det f| (LinearMap.normDet_eq_abs_det).
1. (Fibres as images.) Fix y ∈ ℝ^n. Then g(A) ∩ F^{−1}{y} = g(A ∩ Φ^{−1}{y}). Indeed, if x = g(a) with a ∈ A and F(x) = y, then Φ(a) = F(g(a)) = y, so a ∈ A ∩ Φ^{−1}{y}; conversely, if a ∈ A and Φ(a) = y, then g(a) ∈ g(A) and F(g(a)) = Φ(a) = y.
2. (Reindexing the fibre sum.) g is injective on A ∩ Φ^{−1}{y} ⊆ A (InjOn.mono). By tsum_image (Σ_{x ∈ g(s)} k(x) = Σ_{a ∈ s} k(g(a)) for g injective on s), applied with s := A ∩ Φ^{−1}{y} and k := h, and step 1: Σ_{x ∈ g(A) ∩ F^{−1}{y}} h(x) = Σ_{a ∈ A ∩ Φ^{−1}{y}} h(g(a)). The index subtype A ∩ Φ^{−1}{y} is definitionally {a // a ∈ A ∧ Φ a = y} = areaFiber A Φ y, so the right side is weightedAreaFiberSum A Φ (h∘g) y (rfl). As y was arbitrary, the fibre-sum function y ↦ Σ_{x ∈ g(A) ∩ F^{−1}{y}} h(x) equals weightedAreaFiberSum A Φ (h∘g) (funext).
3. (Hypotheses of (A1).) Φ is Lipschitz, A is Borel, and w := h∘g is Borel measurable because h is Borel measurable and g is continuous, hence measurable (Measurable.comp, Continuous.measurable).
4. (Apply (A1) with E = E' = ℝ^n.) weightedAreaFiberSum A Φ (h∘g) is μHE[finrank ℝ ℝ^n]-a.e. measurable and its integral against μHE[finrank ℝ ℝ^n] equals ∫_A ofReal(areaJacobianAt Φ a) · h(g(a)) dλ(a). By (E) the measure μHE[finrank ℝ ℝ^n] is λ, so by step 2 the fibre-sum function is λ-a.e. measurable (the first assertion) and ∫ Σ_{x ∈ g(A) ∩ F^{−1}{y}} h(x) dλ(y) = ∫_A ofReal(areaJacobianAt Φ a) · h(g(a)) dλ(a).
5. (Jacobian as an absolute determinant.) For every a ∈ ℝ^n, areaJacobianAt Φ a = normDet(DΦ(a)) = |det DΦ(a)| by areaJacobianAt_eq_normDet and (D) applied to the endomorphism DΦ(a) of ℝ^n (this holds whether or not Φ is differentiable at a). Rewriting the integrand pointwise (lintegral_congr) turns the right side of step 4 into ∫_A ofReal(|det DΦ(a)|) · h(g(a)) dλ(a), which is the second assertion. ∎
proof_key_steps: For each y, g(A) ∩ F^{−1}{y} = g(A ∩ Φ^{−1}{y}) because F∘g = Φ on A.
tsum_image (g injective on A ∩ Φ^{−1}{y}) identifies the carrier fibre sum with weightedAreaFiberSum A Φ (h∘g) y.
h∘g is Borel; the SimonGMT Lipschitz weighted area formula (A1) for Φ gives a.e. measurability and ∫ fibre sum dμHE[finrank] = ∫_A ofReal(areaJacobianAt Φ)·h∘g dλ.
μHE[finrank ℝ ℝ^n] = volume and areaJacobianAt Φ a = normDet(DΦ(a)) = |det DΦ(a)| give both assertions.

Converting target Hausdorff measure to volume and normDet to the absolute determinant gives precisely both stated conclusions. No differentiability or measurability hypothesis is silently added, and the proof is complete and non-circular.

subproblem.title: Fibre sums of H^n-a.e. equal weights agree L^n-a.e. (Lipschitz null images; parent step 2)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ; S, V ⊆ ℝ^P with S ⊆ V; G : ℝ^P → ℝ^n Lipschitz (constant L_G); F : ℝ^P → ℝ^n with F = G on V; and h, h' : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] with h = h' almost everywhere for H^n⌞S (H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^P; no measurability of S, h or h' is assumed). Then the fibre-sum functions y ↦ Σ_{x ∈ S, F(x) = y} h(x) and y ↦ Σ_{x ∈ S, F(x) = y} h'(x) on ℝ^n (tsums over the subtype S ∩ F^{−1}{y}) agree for L^n-a.e. y, where L^n = volume on ℝ^n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (S V : Set (Euclid P)) (F G : Euclid P → Euclid n) (LG : NNReal) (h h' : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞), S ⊆ V → LipschitzWith LG G → EqOn F G V → h =ᵐ[μHE[n].restrict S] h' → (fun y : Euclid n => ∑' x : ↥(S ∩ F ⁻¹' {y}), h x) =ᵐ[volume] (fun y : Euclid n => ∑' x : ↥(S ∩ F ⁻¹' {y}), h' x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (reduction to a Borel weight: the set where the weight changes is H^n-null and its image under the map, which agrees with the Lipschitz G there, is L^n-null; Simon Ch. 2 Theorem 1.8(i), Lipschitz images of H^n-null sets are H^n-null). The only change from the parent text is that the disagreement set is enlarged to a Borel H^n⌞S-null set N, so that Measure.restrict_apply applies with N Borel and S need not be Borel (the parent instead used that S = g(A) is Borel). Notation: H^n := μHE[n] (on ℝ^P and on ℝ^n); λ := L^n = volume on ℝ^n; for k : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] and y ∈ ℝ^n, Σ_k(y) := Σ_{x ∈ S ∩ F^{−1}{y}} k(x) ∈ [0, ∞] (tsum over the subtype S ∩ F^{−1}{y}). Library fact (L1): if ψ is K-Lipschitz on a set X, then μHE[n](ψ(X)) ≤ K^n · μHE[n](X) (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn n, applied to LipschitzWith.lipschitzOnWith; available after import GMT.Ch07.Submission). Library fact (E): on ℝ^n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μHE[n] = volume (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume n).
1. (A Borel null set carrying the disagreement.) The hypothesis h = h' (H^n⌞S)-a.e. says (H^n⌞S)({x : h(x) ≠ h'(x)}) = 0 (ae_iff). By exists_measurable_superset_of_null there is a Borel set N ⊇ {x : h(x) ≠ h'(x)} with (H^n⌞S)(N) = 0. Since N is Borel, (H^n⌞S)(N) = H^n(N ∩ S) (Measure.restrict_apply), so H^n(N ∩ S) = 0.
2. (The image of M := N ∩ S is λ-null.) Since M ⊆ S ⊆ V and F = G on V, F and G agree on M, so F(M) = G(M) (Set.image_congr). G is L_G-Lipschitz on ℝ^P, in particular on M, so by (L1) with target ℝ^n, μHE[n](G(M)) ≤ L_G^n · H^n(M) = L_G^n · 0 = 0; hence μHE[n](G(M)) = 0 (le_antisymm with 0 ≤ μHE[n](G(M))). By (E), λ(F(M)) = λ(G(M)) = μHE[n](G(M)) = 0. Therefore λ-a.e. y ∈ ℝ^n satisfies y ∉ F(M) (measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem).
3. (Termwise equality off F(M).) Fix y ∈ ℝ^n with y ∉ F(M), and let x ∈ S with F(x) = y, i.e. x is an element of the index subtype S ∩ F^{−1}{y}. If x ∈ N, then x ∈ N ∩ S = M and y = F(x) ∈ F(M), a contradiction; hence x ∉ N. As {x : h(x) ≠ h'(x)} ⊆ N, it follows that h(x) = h'(x) (by contradiction). Thus the two tsums Σ_h(y) and Σ_{h'}(y) over the same index type S ∩ F^{−1}{y} have equal summands, so Σ_h(y) = Σ_{h'}(y) (tsum_congr).
4. (Conclusion.) By steps 2 and 3, Σ_h(y) = Σ_{h'}(y) for every y outside the λ-null set F(M); i.e. the two fibre-sum functions are equal λ-a.e. (filter_upwards with the a.e. statement of step 2). ∎
proof_key_steps: Enlarge {h ≠ h'} to a Borel set N with (H^n⌞S)(N) = 0; Measure.restrict_apply gives H^n(N ∩ S) = 0.
M := N ∩ S ⊆ V, so F(M) = G(M); (L1) for the Lipschitz G gives μHE[n](G(M)) = 0, and μHE[n] = volume on ℝ^n, so λ(F(M)) = 0.
For y ∉ F(M) every x ∈ S with F(x) = y lies outside N, hence h(x) = h'(x); tsum_congr gives equality of the two fibre sums at y.
Hence the fibre-sum functions agree λ-a.e.

audit.reason: Prose and Lean type match, including the absence of measurability assumptions on S and the weights. The measurable null hull is taken for the restricted measure, so restrict_apply legitimately gives a Hausdorff-null intersection with S. Equality with G and the Lipschitz image bound make its image volume-null; termwise equality then proves equality of the fibre tsums almost everywhere. Every step is justified and non-circular.
